links.outcome: Readability (FRE, Flesch-Kincaid grade level) of ChatGPT tracheostomy care responses versus sixth-grade NIH recommendation
links.effect: FRE mean 39.5 (SD 7.17) and FKRGL mean 13.1 (SD 1.47), college/advanced level, above the sixth-grade level recommended for patient resources.
links.quote: Readability indicated college and advanced levels for FRE (Mean = 39.5, SD = 7.17) and FKRGL (Mean = 13.1, SD = 1.47), higher than the sixth-grade level recommended for patient-targeted resources by the NIH.

links.outcome: Reading level of AI-generated patient-facing responses relative to recommended patient level
links.effect: Responses read at college/advanced levels (FKRGL 13.1, FRE 39.5), above sixth-grade NIH recommendation, potentially limiting patient comprehension.
links.quote: Further, inappropriately high reading levels may limit patient comprehension and accessibility.

links.outcome: Clinical appropriateness and accuracy of ChatGPT tracheostomy care responses graded by otolaryngologists
links.effect: Appropriateness mean 4.10 (SD 0.90) of 5, accuracy 3.55 (SD 0.50) of 4, overall 4.02 (SD 0.86); suboptimal responses lacked nuance and contained incorrect information.
links.quote: Suboptimal responses lacked nuance and contained incorrect information and recommendations.

screen.reason: Evaluates the accuracy, appropriateness, and readability of ChatGPT responses to hypothetical patient tracheostomy care questions without testing a specific deployment practice or guardrail.
